key_insight: Stepped removal of target bias enables self-limiting electrospray deposition to build multiple coating layers with controllable thickness.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to nanoscale, conformal multilayer coatings on complex 3D surfaces without abandoning the benefits of self-limited electrospray processing.
method: Apply electrospray deposition under a target bias to reduce coating thickness and improve uniformity.
Stepwise remove the bias between deposition passes to increment the thickness layer by layer.
Use the approach to form multilayer polystyrene stacks and then infiltrate bilayer films via thermal capillary rise infiltration (CaRI).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful tri-layer polystyrene stacks, uniform tri-layer coatings on a complex geometry, and a mechanically robust nanocomposite made from electrosprayed bilayers with CaRI.
watch_item: Thickness control depends on bias tuning and spray/material parameters, so process repeatability and geometry-specific calibration may be needed.
paper_title: Multilayer Self‐Limiting Electrospray Deposition via Stepped Voltage Bias
